about_blocks.text: EHN Willowview Recovery Centre is a residential addiction treatment centre near Lumsden, about 30 km northwest of Regina. EHN Canada runs it under a service agreement with the Saskatchewan Health Authority, and for eligible Saskatchewan residents the program costs nothing.
about_blocks.html: EHN Willowview Recovery Centre is a residential addiction treatment centre near Lumsden, about 30 km northwest of Regina. EHN Canada runs it under a service agreement with the Saskatchewan Health Authority, and for eligible Saskatchewan residents the program costs nothing.

about_blocks.text: The province calls it Saskatchewan's largest addictions treatment facility. It sits in the renovated former Living Skies Retreat and can take up to 60 clients at a time. The first 20 inpatient spaces opened in January 2025 and the other 40 began intake on April 1, 2025.
about_blocks.html: The province calls it Saskatchewan's largest addictions treatment facility. It sits in the renovated former Living Skies Retreat and can take up to 60 clients at a time. The first 20 inpatient spaces opened in January 2025 and the other 40 began intake on April 1, 2025.

about_blocks.text: The core program runs 8 weeks, and clients can extend for a total of up to 16 weeks in care. EHN lists detox among the parts of treatment, with nurses on site 24/7. Most of the work happens in groups and one-on-one sessions using CBT, DBT and relapse prevention, plus psychoeducation, meditation and breathwork. Counsellors, medical staff and addiction support workers make up the team.

about_blocks.text: EHN says the program includes Indigenous cultural healing practices, family and cultural support, and support for LGBTQ2S+ clients. Clients also have a gym and outdoor activities on the grounds, which look out over the hills of the Qu'Appelle Valley.
about_blocks.html: EHN says the program includes Indigenous cultural healing practices, family and cultural support, and support for LGBTQ2S+ clients. Clients also have a gym and outdoor activities on the grounds, which look out over the hills of the Qu'Appelle Valley.

about_blocks.text: The centre is part of the province's plan to add 500 addiction treatment spaces. The Saskatchewan Health Authority chose EHN through a request for proposals. Opening took longer than planned: Willowview was first expected in spring 2024, and it ran day treatment while fire safety renovations were finished before overnight stays began.

about_blocks.text: You have to be 18 or older, live in Saskatchewan and hold a valid Saskatchewan health card, and the program is meant for people whose main concern is substance use. To apply, you fill out the inquiry form on the EHN website and the admissions team reviews it. After discharge, clients can join the EHN Canada Alumni Association, which keeps in touch with calls, emails and invitations to recovery events.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About EHN Willowview Recovery Centre

faqs.question: Is EHN Willowview Recovery Centre free?

answer_blocks.text: Yes, for Saskatchewan residents. EHN says all programs at Willowview are fully funded by the Saskatchewan Health Authority, so eligible residents pay nothing for treatment. People from outside the province are not accepted at this time.
answer_blocks.html: Yes, for Saskatchewan residents. EHN says all programs at Willowview are fully funded by the Saskatchewan Health Authority, so eligible residents pay nothing for treatment. People from outside the province are not accepted at this time.

answer_blocks.text: Adults 18 and older who live in Saskatchewan and have a valid Saskatchewan health card. The program is for people whose main concern is a substance use disorder.
answer_blocks.html: Adults 18 and older who live in Saskatchewan and have a valid Saskatchewan health card. The program is for people whose main concern is a substance use disorder.

faqs.question: How long is the program at Willowview?

answer_blocks.text: The core residential program is 8 weeks. Clients can extend their stay, up to a total of 16 weeks in care, and the province describes the centre as offering up to 16 weeks of treatment.
answer_blocks.html: The core residential program is 8 weeks. Clients can extend their stay, up to a total of 16 weeks in care, and the province describes the centre as offering up to 16 weeks of treatment.

answer_blocks.text: EHN lists detox as one part of treatment at Willowview, and nurses are on site 24 hours a day. Ask the admissions team how withdrawal would be handled in your situation before you arrive.
answer_blocks.html: EHN lists detox as one part of treatment at Willowview, and nurses are on site 24 hours a day. Ask the admissions team how withdrawal would be handled in your situation before you arrive.

faqs.question: How do I get into Willowview?

answer_blocks.text: Start with the inquiry form on the EHN Willowview web page; the admissions team reviews each form and follows up. You can also call EHN Canada admissions at 1-866-963-6343.

faqs.question: How many people does Willowview treat at once?

answer_blocks.text: Up to 60 clients at a time. The province opened all 60 inpatient spaces in 2025 and calls Willowview the largest addictions treatment facility in Saskatchewan.

faqs.question: What therapies are used at Willowview?

answer_blocks.text: Treatment centres on cognitive behavioural therapy, dialectical behaviour therapy and relapse prevention, delivered in group and one-on-one sessions with psychoeducation. EHN also lists meditation, breathwork, Indigenous cultural healing practices and family and cultural support.

EHN also lists meditation, breathwork, Indigenous cultural healing practices and family and cultural support.

faqs.question: Where is Willowview and how far is it from Regina?

answer_blocks.text: The centre is at 724 Grid Road near Lumsden, in the Qu'Appelle Valley about 30 km northwest of Regina. That is roughly a 30 minute drive from Regina, about an hour from Moose Jaw and around two and a half hours from Saskatoon.

faqs.question: What support is there after Willowview?

answer_blocks.text: Graduates can join the EHN Canada Alumni Association. Members get outreach calls, emails and invitations to special events and recovery celebrations.
